note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — THE HEAD
tiles.details: Existing target photo panel 1 (index 0) genuinely shows the clustered flowering head. Count the lateral racemes and trace their attachment; neither glume veins nor ripe spikelet lengths are resolved in this picture. A compact head alone is not a species identification.
tiles.short: Count 3–20 one-sided flowering racemes on ONE intact stem.

tiles.heading: 02 · BASE AND TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Follow the same plant down to its annual crown; low nodes may root, but the current definitive U. fusca gallery does not expose a connected rooted flowering base. Open species panel 2 (index 1): Jim Conrad's Uvalde photograph ACTUALLY shows the white hair-fringe true ligule across the inner blade–sheath junction. It lacks a physical 1-mm scale, so a calibrated ligule measurement remains a photo gap. Panel 5 (index 4) instead shows tentative Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca spikelets, NOT a ligule or authenticated rooted U. fusca.
tiles.short: Annual base; true ligule is a ~1 mm FRINGE OF HAIRS.
tiles.status: TRUE INNER LIGULE PHOTOGRAPH VERIFIED — SCALE AND ROOTED BASE STILL NEEDED

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE RIPE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Open source-identified Uvalde U. fusca panel 3 (index 2): it REALLY shows intact ribbed, ovoid spikelets on one side of a rachis, but without a ruler or exposed individual glumes. Measure 5–10 ripe attached spikelets at 10–20× with a real millimeter scale; published dimensions are generally ~2.4–3.4 mm, not dimensions certified by panel 3. Panel 5 (index 4) has a ruler but is Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca with tentative taxon identity; NEVER count its measurements as verified U. fusca anatomy.
tiles.short: Usually 2.4–3.0 mm; published variation reaches ~3.4 mm.
tiles.status: REAL ATTACHED SPIKELETS VERIFIED — CALIBRATED EXACT-SPECIES DISSECTION MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE THE BRACTS
tiles.details: Lower glume short relative to spikelet; UT measures ~1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets, so a strict 1/3 cutoff is unsafe. Upper glume near full length. At 10–20× separate both glumes, the cross-veined lower sterile/male lemma and hard transversely wrinkled upper fertile lemma (~2.2–2.9 mm across Kew/AusGrass). Kew reports commonly 5 veins on lower and 7 on upper glume; UT notes lower-glume vein variation. The fertile lemma lacks a conspicuous long awn; a tiny mucro is not one. All measurements are source-based, not current-photo measurements.
tiles.short: Lower glume short but NOT a fixed ≤1/3 rule; upper glume near full length.
tiles.status: DIAGNOSTIC DISSECTION MISSING — NO MICRO ARROWS

tiles.heading: 05 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: REAL DIFFERENT-SPECIES comparisons: panel 7 (index 6) is U. reptans; panels 8–9 (indices 7–8) are U. texana. Do not treat U. fusca's true ligule panel 2 (index 1), attached spikelets panel 3 (index 2), or greenhouse foliage panel 4 (index 3) as look-alikes. Published ripe-spikelet ranges: U. reptans ~1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume ~1/8–1/4; U. fusca ~2.4–3.4 mm with lower glume often ~1/4–1/3 (UT measured glumes may exceed 1/3); U. texana ~4.5–5.9 mm with lower glume ~1/2–2/3. Use actual same-scale measured glumes; if unresolved, label Urochloa sp.
tiles.short: Compare RIPE spikelet length and lower-glume proportion.
tiles.status: REAL LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS — SCALE NOT MATCHED

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: one source-verified same-plant U. fusca rooted annual base and lower node; an additional 1-mm calibrated inner hair-fringe ligule (the unscaled TRUE ligule already exists); 5–10 calibrated mature attached spikelets and dissected lower/upper glumes, lower sterile/male lemma, and hard fertile lemma; matched mature U. reptans/U. texana measurements. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check 7 real JPEGs, 10 teaching panels, 19 preserved existing gross markers, correct 4 definitive/2 tentative/1 NC-held evidence labels, per-photo rights and credits, public filtering, and mobile learner rendering. Do not call the species anatomically FINISHED.
tiles.status: HANDOFF TO PHOTO AND SITE-QA LANES

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: BROWNSEED SIGNALGRASS: begin with several ascending one-sided racemes, then inspect ripe plump blunt spikelets (roughly 2.4–3.4 mm across botanical treatments). Its lower glume is short relative to the spikelet: broad treatments often say ~1/4–1/3, while the UT Central Texas treatment measures ~1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets, sometimes exceeding 1/3. Compare actual glume and spikelet lengths, the true hair-fringe ligule and the annual rooted base; do not infer ratios from the overview photograph.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: BEGIN WITH THE LOCAL TEXAS FIELD PHOTO: Jim Conrad's actual Uvalde flower-bearing plant has long leaves and a branched head with relatively short flower-bearing arms. The roots aren't shown.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Follow the same plant down to its annual crown; low nodes may root, but the current definitive U. fusca gallery does not expose a connected rooted flowering base. Open species panel 2 (index 1): Jim Conrad's Uvalde photograph ACTUALLY shows the white hair-fringe true ligule across the inner blade–sheath junction. It lacks a physical 1-mm scale, so a calibrated ligule measurement remains a photo gap. Panel 5 (index 4) instead shows tentative Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca spikelets, NOT a ligule or authenticated rooted U. fusca.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Open source-identified Uvalde U. fusca panel 3 (index 2): it REALLY shows intact ribbed, ovoid spikelets on one side of a rachis, but without a ruler or exposed individual glumes. Measure 5–10 ripe attached spikelets at 10–20× with a real millimeter scale; published dimensions are generally ~2.4–3.4 mm, not dimensions certified by panel 3. Panel 5 (index 4) has a ruler but is Yucatán Urochloa cf. fusca with tentative taxon identity; NEVER count its measurements as verified U. fusca anatomy.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: A photographed mature spikelet is the test: U. reptans usually 1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume only about 1/8–1/4 of its length, while U. texana is substantially larger (4.5–5.9 mm) and its lower glume normally reaches about half to two-thirds. U. fusca can be rather open or dense depending stage; do not treat head compactness as a yes/no species test.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: BROWNSEED SIGNALGRASS: begin with several ascending one-sided racemes, then inspect ripe plump blunt spikelets (roughly 2.4–3.4 mm across botanical treatments). Its lower glume is short relative to the spikelet: broad treatments often say ~1/4–1/3, while the UT Central Texas treatment measures ~1–1.3 mm on 2.9–3.4 mm spikelets, sometimes exceeding 1/3. Compare actual glume and spikelet lengths, the true hair-fringe ligule and the annual rooted base; do not infer ratios from the overview photograph.
memory_rule: U. reptans tiny ~1.5–2.2 mm and minute basal glume; U. fusca blunt ~2.4–3.4 mm with shorter glume; U. texana much larger ~4.5–5.9 mm with lower glume about half/two-thirds.
safety_note: Actual ligule and attached spikelet images exist and are hosted locally; no physical 1-mm ruler on 2014 Uvalde macro. One NC archived image held from public display; only public-licensed comparisons retained. No full mature measured glume dissection, species-authenticated exposed adventitious roots or mobile Pages QA yet.
field_rule: In the actual Uvalde plant, pair the visible inner white hair-fringe LIGULE with one-sided ovoid attached spikelets; then confirm a mature measured glume/lemma before final species diagnosis. A photo of another Urochloa species is only a comparison.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
